role: Distinct independent raw-first topology challenger; not source extractor or prover
scope: Bounded preread of the exact frozen A/B seal and pinned HFT source; no verdict on any unseen extractor graph or implementation

raw_source.method: Poppler pdftoppm rendering at 150 dpi followed by image inspection; no extracted source graph used

A.kind: Real closed-ball harmonic-extension specialization of the zero-flux fact used by HFT 1.4
A.quantifier_boundary: For n >= 2 and R > 0, an actual harmonic neighborhood extension agreeing with the original function on the parent closed ball is assumed to exist. One such extension is retained and must supply integrable zero radial gradient flux for every 0 < r <= R simultaneously.
important_distinctions: This is not full complex-valued Eq. 1.3 for arbitrary smooth domains.
The original total u is arbitrary off the closed ball. Its derivatives, off-ball regularity and measurability are not conclusions.
The differentiated function in the conclusion is the retained extension witness.
The extension witness called v in the seal is distinct from HFT 1.4's auxiliary radial function also called v.

B.kind: ASTIS canonical-library specification, not a verbatim HFT theorem
B.quantifier_boundary: Every natural dimension, including zero; positive radius; local C1 at each closed-ball point. Both actual coordinate-divergence volume integrability and literal volume.toSphere radial-pairing integrability are conclusions.
important_distinctions: The source states a smooth-domain divergence theorem with geometric outward normal and surface-area measure.
The seal specifies a ball pullback with explicit sphere vector, radius factor and literal polar sphere measure.
No global C1, compact support, boundary identity or integral certificate is a public premise.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed1/PDF9, Definitions and Examples, first paragraph
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The standing dimension is a fixed positive integer greater than one. Harmonicity on an open set means a complex-valued C2 function with the coordinate Laplacian equal to zero.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: A's real-valued and n >= 2 restriction is a specialization. B's dimensions zero and one are outside this standing source range. The source provides second-order regularity, not merely a pointwise Laplace equation without regularity.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed1/PDF9, same paragraph, definition for a not necessarily open set E
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: Harmonicity on E is defined through extension to a harmonic function on an open set containing E.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: Keep an actual extension agreeing on the whole closed ball; do not upgrade an arbitrary total representative to a neighborhood-regular function.

bounded_raw_inventory.observation: Green's identity integrates u Delta(v) minus v Delta(u) over a bounded open smooth-boundary domain. Both scalar functions are C2 on a neighborhood of the closure.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: These conditions belong to the general source theorem. The annulus application in 1.4 still needs its own conditions and cannot be claimed established by a ball-only flux result.

bounded_raw_inventory.observation: V_n is Lebesgue volume; ds is surface-area measure on the boundary; normal differentiation is the gradient paired with the outward unit normal. The text points to Appendix A for ball and sphere integration.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: Neither ds = volume.toSphere nor the ball pullback and its R^(n-1) factor follows from the names of the measures. Appendix A itself was not inspected in this preread.

bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The text invokes the divergence theorem from advanced calculus for a vector field with continuously differentiable components on a neighborhood of the closure. Divergence is the sum of the matching coordinate partial derivatives.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: This is a real mathematical background input, not an identity that can be made true by defining a replacement flux. Complex vector fields are allowed in the source; B is a real specialization with a different explicit boundary representation.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed4/PDF12, sentence following the divergence definition
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The stated derivation of Green's identity uses the vector field u grad(v) minus v grad(u), followed by a computation.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: The source direction is divergence theorem to Green identity. A direct gradient-field ball route may realize the sealed target, but must be labeled separately from the author's displayed derivation.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed4/PDF12, sentence preceding Eq.1.3 and Eq.1.3
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The text obtains zero boundary normal flux when u is harmonic and the second Green-identity function is identically one.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: The harmonicity and regularity/domain hypotheses are inherited, rather than replaced by an assumed zero integral. A is the closed-ball specialization needed for the later two uses.

bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The unit sphere is the boundary of the unit ball. The symbol sigma denotes normalized surface-area measure, with total mass one, and is described as the unique rotation-invariant Borel probability measure.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: Do not identify sigma with the seal's unnormalized tau. Rotation invariance, probability normalization and the area constant are not conclusions of A or B.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed5/PDF13, proof of1.4 through first displayed annulus identity
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: For n > 2 the proof reduces to the unit ball, fixes epsilon in (0,1), and applies Green's identity on epsilon < |x| < 1 with the radial auxiliary function |x|^(2-n).
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: The radial auxiliary function is used on an annulus excluding its singular center. It must not be conflated with A's harmonic extension witness. Domain reduction, kernel properties and the annulus Green step are not proved by A or B.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed5/PDF13, first displayed identity and sentence citing1.3
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The boundary normal-derivative term on the outer unit sphere is asserted to vanish by1.3.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: The outer annulus normal agrees with the filled unit ball's outward radial normal. Record this individual cancellation, its regularity/filled-ball domain and its surface-measure adapter.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed5/PDF13, same identity and same sentence citing1.3
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The normal-derivative term on the inner epsilon sphere is also asserted to vanish by1.3, separately from the outer term.
bounded_raw_inventory.challenge_use: On the inner annulus boundary the outward normal points toward the center. Application of the filled epsilon ball's zero flux therefore needs an explicit normal-sign transport. A single annulus total-flux cancellation does not supply two individual cancellations.

bounded_raw_inventory.anchor: printed5/PDF13, after the two cancellations through end of1.4 proof
bounded_raw_inventory.observation: The source continues with surface scaling/normalization, continuity as epsilon tends to zero, and the n = 2 replacement of the power kernel by log|x|.
bounded_raw_inventory.reason: These are real downstream mean-value proof regions; A supplies zero flux for n >= 2 but does not supply the Green/kernel, scaling-to-sigma or limiting steps. Exclusion here is not a claim that the full1.4 proof has been covered.

bounded_raw_inventory.reason: The examples and rotation statement are not used by the sealed flux targets or the two zero-flux use sites. The following volume mean-value paragraph is a different downstream result.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.required_review_evidence: Keep the source theorem, ASTIS library specification and consumer specialization as distinct records with explicit adapters. Do not inflate A/B into coverage of all smooth-boundary geometry or full HFT1.4.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.concern: The raw source uses geometric surface-area ds, whereas the seal fixes literal volume.toSphere tau and the radius factor R^(n-1). Their identification and change of variables are not present on the inspected pages.
critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.required_review_evidence: An explicit bridge for the volume convention, unit-sphere measure, translation and positive dilation, including the exact exponent and no unexplained probability or area constant. An implementation route that proves B directly must distinguish this from a source-given surface transport theorem.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.concern: The explicit vector zeta in A/B has to match the geometric outward normal of the filled ball. It has the opposite sign from the outward annulus normal on the inner boundary in1.4.
critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.required_review_evidence: Separate normal-identification and inner-boundary sign adapters; two explicit1.3 cancellation use sites. Do not replace the pair by one total annulus flux identity.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.required_review_evidence: Independent dependency content deriving actual integrability from local regularity, compact geometry and finite relevant measures. No public integrability, shell estimate or boundary identity may be added as a convenience premise.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.concern: B assumes C1 locally at every closed-ball point. The source states C1 on a neighborhood of the whole closure. A review must account for the passage between those formulations without silently requiring global C1 or compact support.

Preserve the exact pointwise closed-ball binder; make any C1 assertion about the gradient extension an internally discharged consequence of harmonic regularity.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.concern: A must retain one actual extension before quantifying over all positive subradii. A collection of radius-dependent witnesses or a regularity claim for the arbitrary total u would not match the seal.
critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.required_review_evidence: The same witness agrees on the parent closed ball and supplies every subball flux, including r = R. Derivatives remain derivatives of that witness. Closed-ball equality alone gives no neighborhood regularity to arbitrary off-ball u.

critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.concern: The raw HFT convention n > 1 does not cover B at n = 0 or n = 1. Dimension zero also exposes the empty unit sphere, zero-coordinate divergence and natural-number subtraction in n - 1.
critical_concerns_frozen_before_extracto.required_review_evidence: A candid library-specific treatment of these dimensions with literal measure and divergence semantics. No hidden positive-dimension assumption or appeal to HFT's standing convention may remove them. This preread does not certify the degenerate cases.
